functions.name: xnn_initialize
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_initialize(const struct xnn_allocator* allocator);
functions.description: Initialize the XNNPACK library and its microkernel/architecture-specific tables. Pass a custom allocator or NULL to use system malloc/free. Must be called successfully before using other XNNPACK APIs.
requirements: Must be called before any other XNNPACK API that requires initialization.
allocator may be NULL, in which case system allocation routines are used.
On failure, check returned xnn_status for out-of-memory or unsupported hardware and avoid subsequent calls that assume initialization.

functions.name: xnn_deinitialize
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_deinitialize(void);
functions.description: Deinitialize XNNPACK. Currently a no-op but provided for symmetry and future-proofing.
requirements: Safe to call after successful xnn_initialize.
Return value should be checked for xnn_status_success.

functions.name: xnn_experimental_get_build_identifier_data
functions.signature: const void* xnn_experimental_get_build_identifier_data();
functions.description: Return a pointer to internal data that uniquely identifies the set of microkernel implementations in this build. Intended for comparing/validating packed-weights or kernel compatibility across runs.
requirements: Returned pointer is owned by XNNPACK; treat as read-only.
Use together with xnn_experimental_get_build_identifier_size to know its length.
Pointer remains valid as long as the library is loaded; do not free.

functions.name: xnn_experimental_get_build_identifier_size
functions.signature: size_t xnn_experimental_get_build_identifier_size();
functions.description: Return the size in bytes of the build-identifier data returned by xnn_experimental_get_build_identifier_data.
requirements: Call to size must be paired with reading exactly that many bytes from the data pointer returned by xnn_experimental_get_build_identifier_data.

functions.name: xnn_experimental_check_build_identifier
functions.signature: bool xnn_experimental_check_build_identifier(const void* data, size_t size);
functions.description: Check whether the provided identifier blob matches the identifier of the currently loaded build. Useful to verify compatibility of cached packed weights.
requirements: data must point to a buffer of length size bytes.
size must equal xnn_experimental_get_build_identifier_size() for a successful comparison.
Returns true on exact match; false otherwise.

functions.name: xnn_create_subgraph
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_create_subgraph(uint32_t external_value_ids, uint32_t flags, xnn_subgraph_t* subgraph_out);
functions.description: Create an empty Subgraph object used to define tensors (Values) and operators (Nodes). Optionally reserve a range of external Value IDs for integration with an external graph representation.
requirements: subgraph_out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the handle.
external_value_ids indicates the size of the reserved external ID range [0, external_value_ids-1].
flags currently has no supported bits; pass 0.
Check return status before using the output handle.

functions.name: xnn_delete_subgraph
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_delete_subgraph(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph);
functions.description: Destroy a Subgraph and all Values and Nodes it owns.
requirements: subgraph must be a valid handle returned by xnn_create_subgraph or NULL (behavior for NULL not specified; treat non-NULL expected).
Do not use the handle after deletion.
Ensure any dependent Runtime objects are not relying on this subgraph (runtimes are independent once constructed).

functions.name: xnn_define_tensor_value
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_tensor_value(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, enum xnn_datatype datatype, size_t num_dims, const size_t* dims, const void* data, uint32_t external_id, uint32_t flags, uint32_t* id_out);
functions.description: Define a dense tensor Value in a Subgraph. Can optionally provide static initialization data and/or assign an external ID for IO mapping.
requirements: subgraph must be a valid Subgraph handle.
datatype must be one of enum xnn_datatype and not xnn_datatype_invalid.
num_dims can be 0; if >0 then dims must point to an array of num_dims elements.
If data is non-NULL, its lifetime must outlive the Subgraph and any Runtimes created from it.
external_id must be XNN_INVALID_VALUE_ID to auto-assign, or be within the reserved [0, external_value_ids-1] range from subgraph creation.
flags may combine XNN_VALUE_FLAG_EXTERNAL_INPUT and/or XNN_VALUE_FLAG_EXTERNAL_OUTPUT.
id_out must be non-NULL to receive the assigned Value ID.

functions.name: xnn_define_quantized_tensor_value
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_quantized_tensor_value(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, enum xnn_datatype datatype, int32_t zero_point, float scale, size_t num_dims, const size_t* dims, const void* data, uint32_t external_id, uint32_t flags, uint32_t* id_out);
functions.description: Define a per-tensor quantized Value with zero_point and scale in a Subgraph. Supports various quantized datatypes (e.g., qint8/quint8/qint32).
requirements: subgraph must be valid.
datatype must be a supported quantized type (per function intent; header does not enumerate here).
scale is a floating-point multiplier; must be positive (implied by typical quantization; exact constraint not explicitly stated).
num_dims/dims same rules as xnn_define_tensor_value.
If data is non-NULL, its lifetime must outlive Subgraph/Runtime.
external_id rules as in xnn_define_tensor_value.
flags supports XNN_VALUE_FLAG_EXTERNAL_INPUT/OUTPUT.
id_out must be non-NULL.

functions.name: xnn_define_channelwise_quantized_tensor_value
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_channelwise_quantized_tensor_value(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, enum xnn_datatype datatype, const float* scale, size_t num_dims, size_t channel_dim, const size_t* dims, const void* data, uint32_t external_id, uint32_t flags, uint32_t* id_out);
functions.description: Define a per-channel quantized Value where each channel (along channel_dim) has its own scale. Zero-point handling is implicit/absent in this variant.
requirements: subgraph must be valid.
datatype must be a supported per-channel quantized type (e.g., qcint8/qcint32/qcint4/qcint2).
scale must point to an array sized to the length of the channel_dim; lifetime must outlive Subgraph/Runtime if used for static initialization.
num_dims/dims define the tensor shape; dims must be non-NULL if num_dims>0.
channel_dim must be a valid axis index (< num_dims).
data/external_id/flags/id_out follow rules as in xnn_define_tensor_value.

functions.name: xnn_validate_quantized_tensor
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_validate_quantized_tensor(enum xnn_datatype datatype, int32_t zero_point, float scale, size_t num_dims, const size_t* dims);
functions.description: Validate that quantized tensor metadata (datatype, zero_point, scale, shape) is acceptable. This does not create a Value; it only checks parameters.
requirements: datatype must be a quantized datatype.
num_dims and dims must be consistent (dims can be NULL only if num_dims==0).
Callers should ensure scale is a positive finite value; header implies typical quantization semantics though not explicitly stated.
Use return status to determine validity before defining a Value.

functions.name: xnn_validate_channelwise_quantized_tensor
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_validate_channelwise_quantized_tensor(enum xnn_datatype datatype, int32_t zero_point, const float* scale, size_t num_dims, size_t channel_dim, const size_t* dims);
functions.description: Validate per-channel quantized tensor metadata (datatype, zero_point, per-channel scales, shape and channel axis).
requirements: datatype must be a per-channel quantized datatype supported by XNNPACK.
scale must be non-NULL and contain as many entries as the size of dims[channel_dim].
channel_dim must be < num_dims.
dims must be non-NULL if num_dims>0.
Zero point semantics apply per overall tensor; specific constraints are implementation-defined.

functions.name: xnn_define_channelwise_quantized_tensor_value_v3
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_channelwise_quantized_tensor_value_v3(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, enum xnn_datatype datatype, int32_t zero_point, const float* scale, size_t num_dims, size_t channel_dim, const size_t* dims, const void* data, uint32_t external_id, uint32_t flags, uint32_t* id_out, const float* channelwise_zero_point);
functions.description: Define a per-channel quantized Value with a tensor-level zero_point, per-channel scales, and an optional per-channel zero-point array. Adds the Value to the Subgraph.
requirements: subgraph must be valid.
datatype must support channelwise quantization.
scale must have length equal to dims[channel_dim].
If channelwise_zero_point is provided, it must have length equal to dims[channel_dim].
num_dims/dims and channel_dim must be consistent.
data/external_id/flags/id_out follow rules as in xnn_define_tensor_value.
Static data and parameter arrays must outlive Subgraph/Runtime if referenced.

functions.name: xnn_define_channelwise_quantized_tensor_value_v2
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_channelwise_quantized_tensor_value_v2(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, enum xnn_datatype datatype, int32_t zero_point, const float* scale, size_t num_dims, size_t channel_dim, const size_t* dims, const void* data, uint32_t external_id, uint32_t flags, uint32_t* id_out);
functions.description: Define a per-channel quantized Value with a tensor-level zero_point and per-channel scales (no per-channel zero-points).
requirements: Same structural requirements as v3 without channelwise_zero_point.
scale length must match dims[channel_dim].
All pointer lifetimes (data/scale) must outlive Subgraph/Runtime where applicable.

functions.name: xnn_define_blockwise_quantized_tensor_value_v2
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_blockwise_quantized_tensor_value_v2(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, enum xnn_datatype datatype, int32_t zero_point, const void* scale, size_t num_dims, size_t channel_dim, size_t block_size, const size_t* dims, const void* data, uint32_t external_id, uint32_t flags, enum xnn_datatype scale_type, uint32_t* id_out);
functions.description: Define a blockwise-quantized Value where each output channel has per-block scale parameters (e.g., for FC with 2D filters). scale_type indicates the datatype of the encoded scales (bf6/fp16 supported; only 7 mantissa bits used).
requirements: subgraph must be valid.
datatype must be a supported blockwise quantized type.
block_size must be >= XNN_MIN_BLOCKSIZE (32).
channel_dim must indicate the channel axis to which per-block quantization applies.
For FC filters shaped [OC, IC], the number of scale values must equal OC * (IC / block_size).
scale must point to properly typed data per scale_type; lifetime must outlive Subgraph/Runtime if referenced.
num_dims/dims consistent; data/external_id/flags/id_out rules as in xnn_define_tensor_value.

functions.name: xnn_define_blockwise_quantized_tensor_value
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_blockwise_quantized_tensor_value(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, enum xnn_datatype datatype, int32_t zero_point, const uint16_t* scale, size_t num_dims, size_t channel_dim, size_t block_size, const size_t* dims, const void* data, uint32_t external_id, uint32_t flags, uint32_t* id_out);
functions.description: Legacy/first version of blockwise-quantized Value definition using 16-bit encoded scales (e.g., fp16/bf6 encoded in uint16).
requirements: Same structural requirements as v2. Scale data must be a uint16_t array sized per channel and block arrangement.
block_size should align with XNN_MIN_BLOCKSIZE and tensor layout expectations.

functions.name: xnn_define_dynamically_quantized_tensor_value
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_dynamically_quantized_tensor_value(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, enum xnn_datatype datatype, size_t num_dims, size_t num_nonbatch_dims, const size_t* dims, uint32_t external_id, uint32_t flags, uint32_t* id_out);
functions.description: Define a dynamically-quantized Value where per-batch quantization parameters are computed at runtime. The leading (num_dims - num_nonbatch_dims) dimensions form the batch.
requirements: subgraph must be valid.
datatype must be a supported dynamic quantized type (e.g., qdint8/qpint8 etc., per library semantics).
num_nonbatch_dims must be <= num_dims; batch is the flattened product of leading dims.
dims rules as usual: non-NULL if num_dims>0.
external_id/flags/id_out follow standard rules.

functions.name: xnn_define_unary
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_unary(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, enum xnn_unary_operator type, const union xnn_unary_params* params, uint32_t input_id, uint32_t output_id, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Define a unary elementwise Node (e.g., abs, gelu, clamp, convert, etc.) that maps one input Value to one output Value of the same shape. Parameters are interpreted per operator type.
requirements: subgraph must be valid and contain previously defined Values with IDs input_id and output_id.
Input and output shapes must match (same rank and dims).
type must be a valid enum xnn_unary_operator.
params may be NULL if not required by the chosen operator; when provided, fields must match the operator (e.g., clamp.min/max, elu.alpha, leaky_relu.negative_slope).
flags currently have no supported bits; pass 0.

functions.name: xnn_define_convert
functions.signature: XNN_DEPRECATED enum xnn_status xnn_define_convert(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, uint32_t input_id, uint32_t output_id, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Define a deprecated Convert Node that casts data types elementwise while preserving shape.
requirements: Deprecated API; prefer xnn_define_unary with xnn_unary_convert.
Input and output tensors must be defined in the same subgraph and have identical shape.
flags: none supported.

functions.name: xnn_define_convolution_2d
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_convolution_2d(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, uint32_t input_padding_top, uint32_t input_padding_right, uint32_t input_padding_bottom, uint32_t input_padding_left, uint32_t kernel_height, uint32_t kernel_width, uint32_t subsampling_height, uint32_t subsampling_width, uint32_t dilation_height, uint32_t dilation_width, uint32_t groups, size_t group_input_channels, size_t group_output_channels, float output_min, float output_max, uint32_t input_id, uint32_t filter_id, uint32_t bias_id, uint32_t output_id, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Define a 2D convolution Node with optional bias, grouping, stride (subsampling), and dilation. Input/output are NHWC 4D tensors; filter is grouped OIHW in NHWC-style order per docs.
requirements: If flags includes XNN_FLAG_TENSORFLOW_SAME_PADDING, all input paddings must be 0 (padding computed dynamically).
Input must be 4D [N, IH, IW, groups*group_input_channels].
Filter must be 4D [groups*group_output_channels, kernel_height, kernel_width, group_input_channels].
bias_id may be XNN_INVALID_VALUE_ID for no bias; otherwise bias must be 1D [groups*group_output_channels].
Output must be 4D [N, OH, OW, groups*group_output_channels].
output_min <= output_max expected; used for clamp/activation range.
groups >= 1; channel counts must be consistent with Value shapes.
flags currently supports XNN_FLAG_TENSORFLOW_SAME_PADDING only.

functions.name: xnn_define_deconvolution_2d
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_deconvolution_2d(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, uint32_t padding_top, uint32_t padding_right, uint32_t padding_bottom, uint32_t padding_left, uint32_t adjustment_height, uint32_t adjustment_width, uint32_t kernel_height, uint32_t kernel_width, uint32_t upsampling_height, uint32_t upsampling_width, uint32_t dilation_height, uint32_t dilation_width, uint32_t groups, size_t group_input_channels, size_t group_output_channels, float output_min, float output_max, uint32_t input_id, uint32_t filter_id, uint32_t bias_id, uint32_t output_id, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Define a 2D transposed convolution (deconvolution) Node with upsampling stride, dilation, grouping, and optional bias. Shapes mirror convolution but account for transposed operation.
requirements: Input must be 4D [N, IH, IW, groups*group_input_channels].
Filter must be 4D [groups*group_output_channels, kernel_height, kernel_width, group_input_channels].
Bias optional (XNN_INVALID_VALUE_ID) or 1D [groups*group_output_channels].
Output must be 4D [N, OH, OW, groups*group_output_channels].
padding_* specify padding on the output feature map domain.
adjustment_height/width allow additional elements on bottom/right.
flags: no supported flags currently.

functions.name: xnn_define_depthwise_convolution_2d
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_depthwise_convolution_2d(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, uint32_t input_padding_top, uint32_t input_padding_right, uint32_t input_padding_bottom, uint32_t input_padding_left, uint32_t kernel_height, uint32_t kernel_width, uint32_t subsampling_height, uint32_t subsampling_width, uint32_t dilation_height, uint32_t dilation_width, uint32_t depth_multiplier, size_t input_channels, float output_min, float output_max, uint32_t input_id, uint32_t filter_id, uint32_t bias_id, uint32_t output_id, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Define a 2D depthwise convolution Node (per-channel convolution with depth_multiplier). Filter uses HWGo-like layout implied by depthwise mode.
requirements: If flags includes XNN_FLAG_TENSORFLOW_SAME_PADDING, all input paddings must be 0.
Input is 4D [N, IH, IW, input_channels].
Filter is 4D [1, kernel_height, kernel_width, input_channels * depth_multiplier].
Bias optional or 1D [input_channels * depth_multiplier].
Output is 4D [N, OH, OW, input_channels * depth_multiplier].
output_min/max define clamp range.
flags supports XNN_FLAG_TENSORFLOW_SAME_PADDING.

functions.name: xnn_define_depth_to_space_2d
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_depth_to_space_2d(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, uint32_t block_size, uint32_t input_id, uint32_t output_id, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Define a Depth-to-Space 2D Node (NHWC) that reorganizes channel data into spatial blocks by factor block_size.
requirements: Input is 4D [N, IH, IW, OC * block_size * block_size].
Output is 4D [N, IH * block_size, IW * block_size, OC].
block_size must be > 0.
flags: none supported.

functions.name: xnn_define_depth_to_space
functions.signature: enum xnn_status xnn_define_depth_to_space(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, uint32_t input_id, uint32_t output_id, uint32_t block_size, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Define a Depth-to-Space Node with argument order (input, output, block_size). Functionally equivalent to xnn_define_depth_to_space_2d.
requirements: Same as xnn_define_depth_to_space_2d; ensure shapes match transformation.
flags: none supported.

functions.name: xnn_define_global_average_pooling_1d
functions.signature: XNN_DEPRECATED enum xnn_status xnn_define_global_average_pooling_1d(xnn_subgraph_t subgraph, float output_min, float output_max, uint32_t input_id, uint32_t output_id, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Define a deprecated Global Average Pooling over the second-innermost dimension of an N>=2-D dense tensor (keep-dims optional).
requirements: Input must have at least 2 dims; reduction over the second-innermost dimension.
Output must be same-rank if XNN_FLAG_KEEP_DIMS is set; otherwise reduced rank by 1 along that axis.
output_min/max define clamp range.
flags supports XNN_FLAG_KEEP_DIMS.
Deprecated API.

functions.name: xnn_define_global_average_pooling_2d
functions.signature:
XNN_DEPRECATED enum xnn_status xnn_define_global_average_pooling_2d(
  xnn_subgraph_t subgraph,
  float output_min,
  float output_max,
  uint32_t input_id,
  uint32_t output_id,
  uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Adds a deprecated 2D global average pooling node to a subgraph. Computes mean over the two innermost spatial dimensions of the input tensor and writes to the output tensor, optionally clamped to [output_min, output_max]. Use for NHWC-like tensors with ≥3 dims. Prefer newer APIs where available.
requirements: subgraph must be a valid created subgraph
input_id must refer to a dense tensor with 3 or more dimensions defined in subgraph; reduction is over the second- and third-innermost dims
output_id must refer to a dense tensor with 3 or more dimensions defined in subgraph
flags: only XNN_FLAG_KEEP_DIMS is supported; otherwise reduced rank expected
output_min <= output_max (implied by clamping semantics)
Function is deprecated per header comments

functions.name: xnn_define_global_sum_pooling_1d
functions.signature:
XNN_DEPRECATED enum xnn_status xnn_define_global_sum_pooling_1d(
  xnn_subgraph_t subgraph,
  float output_min,
  float output_max,
  uint32_t input_id,
  uint32_t output_id,
  uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Adds a deprecated 1D global sum pooling node to a subgraph. Sums over the second-innermost dimension of the input tensor (channels preserved), with optional output clamping.
requirements: subgraph must be valid
input_id must refer to a dense tensor with 2 or more dimensions defined in subgraph; reduction is across second-innermost dimension
output_id must refer to a dense tensor with 2 or more dimensions defined in subgraph
flags: only XNN_FLAG_KEEP_DIMS is supported
output_min and output_max define clamp bounds; output_min <= output_max (implied)
Deprecated per header

functions.name: xnn_define_global_sum_pooling_2d
functions.signature:
XNN_DEPRECATED enum xnn_status xnn_define_global_sum_pooling_2d(
  xnn_subgraph_t subgraph,
  float output_min,
  float output_max,
  uint32_t input_id,

data_types.description: An opaque byte sequence with no required structure or encoding. May contain any values (including null bytes). Used as a raw blob passed with its length to APIs that compare or process binary identifiers.

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target data type: arbitrary binary data (opaque blob)
# Used by xnn_experimental_check_build_identifier(data, size)
# Strategy:
# - Generate a variety of plausible sizes and byte patterns to exercise both
#   matching and non-matching cases in the fuzzer stub. While we cannot know the
#   library's real build identifier at generation time, we can construct inputs
#   that are likely to explore different code paths:
#   * Empty blob (size==0)
#   * Very small blobs (1-16 bytes)
#   * Medium blobs (17-256 bytes)
#   * Larger blobs (257-2048 bytes)
#   * Structured-looking blobs (repeated patterns, incremental counters)
#   * Random blobs
#   * Mixed content: ASCII-like headers followed by binary tail
# - Ensure deterministic randomness from the provided seed.
# - Keep size under 4096 bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _pattern_repeat(rng: random.Random, unit: bytes, total: int) -> bytes:
    if not unit:
        return b""
    reps = total // len(unit)
    rem = total % len(unit)
    return unit * reps + unit[:rem]


def _make_structured_blob(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a header with a magic, version, length, and checksum-like field,
    # then fill payload with patterned data. Although the API treats data as
    # opaque, such structure can trigger different memcmp lengths and code paths.
    # Header layout (16 bytes):
    #   0-3  : magic 'XNN\0'
    #   4    : version (0..7)
    #   5-7  : reserved
    #   8-11 : claimed_size (uint32, may match actual size with some probability)
    #   12-15: sum32 of payload (little-endian)
    header_size = 16
    if size < header_size:
        # Fall back to random
        return _rand_bytes(rng, size)

    magic = b"XNN\x00"
    version = rng.randrange(0, 8)
    reserved = bytes([0, 0, 0])

    # Decide whether to claim the exact size or a nearby value
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        claimed = size
    else:
        delta = rng.randint(-8, 8)
        claimed = max(0, min(MAX_SIZE, size + delta))

    payload_len = size - header_size

    # Create a patterned payload: mix of counter, repeats, and random tail
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # 1) Counter block
    counter_block_len = rng.randint(0, max(0, payload_len // 3))
    counter = bytearray()
    val = rng.randrange(256)
    for _ in range(counter_block_len):
        counter.append(val & 0xFF)
        val = (val + 1) & 0xFF
    parts.append(bytes(counter))

    remaining = payload_len - len(counter)
    # 2) Repeated pattern block
    rep_block_len = rng.randint(0, max(0, remaining))
    unit_len = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16])
    unit = _rand_bytes(rng, unit_len)
    parts.append(_pattern_repeat(rng, unit, rep_block_len))

    remaining = payload_len - sum(len(p) for p in parts)
    # 3) Random tail
    if remaining > 0:
        parts.append(_rand_bytes(rng, remaining))

    payload = b"".join(parts)
    sum32 = sum(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF

    header = (
        magic
        + bytes([version])
        + reserved
        + struct.pack("<I", claimed)
        + struct.pack("<I", sum32)
    )
    return header + payload


def _make_texty_blob(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    # Create a blob that begins with plausible ASCII text lines and then binary.
    if size == 0:
        return b""
    ascii_lines = []
    # Common headers/keys
    candidates = [
        b"XNNPACK\n",
        b"BUILD_ID=",
        b"version=",
        b"arch=",
        b"microkernels=",
        b"timestamp=",
    ]
    target_header = rng.choice(candidates)
    line = target_header + _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(4, 24)).hex().encode("ascii") + b"\n"
    ascii_lines.append(line)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        ascii_lines.append(b"identifier:\n")
    head = b"".join(ascii_lines)
    if len(head) >= size:
        return head[:size]
    tail = _rand_bytes(rng, size - len(head))
    return head + tail


def _choose_size(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Weighted choice of sizes
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.10:
        return 0
    elif roll < 0.30:
        return rng.randint(1, 16)
    elif roll < 0.70:
        return rng.randint(17, 256)
    elif roll < 0.95:
        return rng.randint(257, 2048)
    else:
        return rng.randint(2049, min(3072, MAX_SIZE))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    size = _choose_size(rng)

    # Choose a construction strategy
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.20:
        # Pure random
        blob = _rand_bytes(rng, size)
    elif mode < 0.40:
        # Repeated unit pattern
        unit_len = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 32])
        unit = _rand_bytes(rng, unit_len)
        blob = _pattern_repeat(rng, unit, size)
    elif mode < 0.60:
        # Structured header + payload
        blob = _make_structured_blob(rng, size)
    elif mode < 0.80:
        # Text-like prefix
        blob = _make_texty_blob(rng, size)
    else:
        # Mixed blocks: [random][pattern][random]
        a = rng.randint(0, size)
        b = rng.randint(0, size - a)
        c = size - a - b
        unit = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.choice([1, 2, 4, 8, 16]))
        blob = _rand_bytes(rng, a) + _pattern_repeat(rng, unit, b) + _rand_bytes(rng, c)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(blob) > MAX_SIZE:
        blob = blob[:MAX_SIZE]

    return blob
